review_scope: Static receipt controller review only; not Desktop/provider/list product acceptance. Reviewer authored original r308 helper; proposed debug extension and Go3 runner are by Source. No independent reacceptance of old helper claimed.

findings.title: Post-launch exceptions escape without a complete failure receipt
findings.fact: No exception/finally envelope protects run_owned call, post-run runtime enumeration, all hash checks, UTF-8 output parsing, summary or manifest. A Python failure at 110/114/118 aborts before summary/manifest. An unexpected helper raise bypasses owned-child recording. Preflight failures have no durable failure origin either.
findings.required_change: Use a fresh exclusive once/output claim before fallible execution preparation; save actual invocation and nullable result/raw in finally, immediately preserve the first stage/error/native unknown separately, then attempt independent after-vector/cleanup facts without replacing the original failure. No retry or guessed native exit. Existing output must never be overwritten.

findings.title: Fixed source SHA is not the actual Python loader/authorization closure
findings.fact: The runner does not require no_site/isolated/UTF8 or disable bytecode writes. SourceFileLoader.exec_module may consume cached bytecode instead of the previously hashed source. python_inputs only records files after imports; it does not establish that unapproved site inputs were excluded. New grant/spec/compiled-evidence control refs are checked before execution but are not explicitly included in the after-protected vector.
findings.required_change: Pin launcher Python and -I -S -X utf8, check flags; disable pyc writes and execute exact verified helper bytes via compile into a module. Bind actual controller/grant/spec/helper and all consumed immutable refs in before/after closure, including loaded __file__/existing __cached__/DLL observations. Keep Python point-in-time limitation explicit; no site-packages expansion or claim of lifecycle capture.

findings.title: Hash phases exceed the declared owned timeout without recording timeout
findings.fact: Synchronous module ReadFile loop and final retained-handle rehash contain no deadline checks. The timeout is only tested between pump calls; post-exit rehash is entirely outside that check. Up to 1 GiB before plus after hashes can therefore finish after150s with timed_out false. Failure cleanup pumping may also process/continue notifications, while final rehash extends beyond declared5s termination observation.
findings.required_change: Pass explicit monotonic deadlines through capture/hash/posthash, preserve incomplete evidence on deadline, and distinguish child termination observation from evidence-finalization time. For a hard outer bound on blocking WinAPI/file reads, specify an owned outer controller process/Job and exact cleanup behavior; do not claim existing150+5 as total wall bound. Do not loosen tests120s or silently omit module hashes.

findings.title: Debug capture success lacks the finite process/event invariants
findings.fact: DEBUG_ONLY_THIS_PROCESS does not collect descendant DLL events, but ACCOUNTING.TotalProcesses is not retained or constrained to1. complete only requires nonempty modules and an exit event. It does not require exactly one CREATE_PROCESS image matching pinned983f executable, one exit code consistent with the held process result, or reject RIP/unrecognized events. The first breakpoint code is swallowed regardless of first_chance. Runner success does not explicitly require resumed/assigned_before_resume/kill_on_job_close.
findings.required_change: For this one-process component reject TotalProcesses!=1, require ordered unique primary CREATE_PROCESS and EXIT_PROCESS with exact pinned image and independent exit agreement, reject unsupported/RIP observations, constrain/document the initial loader breakpoint rule, and assert all existing owned-Job success fields. Continue received owned events in finally on failure; document debug-event process/thread handle lifetime versus explicitly owned CreateProcess/file handles, avoiding premature close or double close. These are proposed guards, not claims a native violation was observed.

supported_design: New receipt helper preserves r308 original bytes and its prohibition on caller-provided debug/breakaway flags. Fixed DEBUG_ONLY_THIS_PROCESS added only to new helper.
CreateProcess suspended -> creation time -> assign exclusive kill-on-close Job -> resume; std handle-list duplicates are explicit.
Actual event hFile is duplicated, read and retained; null/unreadable hFile fails closed instead of falling back to guessed paths or PE import lists.
x64 decoder declared union offset16,size176 and exception first_chance offset152; no native ABI execution performed here.
Other exceptions use DBG_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED; actual termination request versus observed exit remain separate.
The proposal explicitly discloses debugger timing changes and Python point-in-time inventory limitation.
limitations: Existing983f binary identity and old64PASS do not prove a new debug-mode run passed. All future3 selectors remain NOT_RUN.
Python before/after module inventory cannot establish absence of transient loads/unloads. This review does not upgrade it to whole-lifecycle proof.
Windows debug-event handle closure semantics must be explicitly documented in revised helper; this review does not assert an observed native handle leak.
No rehash of all8577 compilation inputs in this static review; proposal manifest source bytes verified.
